title: Crude Oil Margin Pressure Monitor

channels.limitations: Crude-to-diesel pass-through varies with refining spreads, inventory and contract pricing.

indicators: BLS producer price indexes for chemicals and plastics
channels.limitations: Input costs differ by feedstock, natural gas prices, geography and hedging.
Demand response depends on income, savings, wage growth and substitution.

hypotheses.claim: Sustained higher petroleum-related costs may pressure margins for firms unable to pass costs to customers
hypotheses.test: Compare sector-level gross margins and earnings guidance with lagged oil and diesel prices, controlling for demand and hedging.

hypotheses.claim: Energy-sector buying can partly offset non-energy declines in a capitalization-weighted index
hypotheses.test: Decompose SPY daily return into sector contribution using contemporaneous index weights and returns.

warnings: Do not equate oil price level with an observed margin decline.
Do not assume energy sector has exactly ten S&P 500 constituents.
Do not infer intentional index support from sector return attribution.
